headline: AMD reinstates TSME on Ryzen 9000 CPUs in July
summary: AMD to bring back Transparent Secure Memory Encryption on non-PRO Ryzen 9000 processors
details: AMD will reinstate Transparent Secure Memory Encryption (TSME) on desktop Ryzen 9000 processors in July. The feature is branded as Memory Guard for AMD's Ryzen PRO lineup, but it's available on non-PRO CPUs, as well.
TSME is a firmware-level encryption feature for memory. It allows the processor to generate a key in order to encrypt data stored in RAM, serving as a layer of protection against cold boot attacks.

The feature was quietly removed through a firmware update on some non-PRO Ryzen CPUs. AMD tells Tom's Hardware that it's bringing TSME back to non-PRO Ryzen 9000 chips 'based on valuable community feedback.'

headline_marked: Developer builds [[Proximo]] AI for secure Proxmox cluster management
headline: Developer builds Proximo AI for secure Proxmox cluster management
summary: Proximo is an open-source AI for Proxmox clusters with transparent management
details: A developer created Proximo, an open-source AI agent for managing Proxmox clusters. It allows for full management with a trust model built-in.
Proximo requires approval for actions before they are executed, providing a layer of security and transparency. It uses the Proxmox REST API with a scoped token.
The AI agent was built with the help of Claude, Anthropic's model, and Maude, a Claude-helper plugin. It's available on GitHub under the Apache-2.0 license.
caption:
Can you trust an AI to manage your Proxmox cluster?

A developer created Proximo, an open-source AI agent for managing Proxmox clusters. It allows for full management with a trust model built-in.
